strategies.outdated: This analysis was written prior to Miraidon's ban. As such, the information provided is out of date and does not accurately reflect the current metagame. Bear with us while we rework our analyses!
strategies.overview: Flutter Mane carves itself a niche as one of the most threatening wallbreakers in Ubers thanks to its incredibly powerful STAB combination, near-unrivaled Speed that is boosted further under sun, good coverage options, and great defensive typing, allowing it to operate as a solid revenge killer against Pokemon like Extreme Killer Arceus. Its Ghost / Fairy typing allows it to target a variety of threats, particularly the big three Pokemon in the tier—Miraidon, Koraidon, and Necrozma-DM— as well as Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Extreme Killer Arceus. However, Flutter Mane struggles to find opportunities to switch in safely thanks to its mediocre physical bulk and vulnerability to entry hazards. Likewise, some special walls like Ho-Oh and Arceus-Water can take an attack and potentially threaten to status Flutter Mane or flat out KO it.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
Psyshock is Flutter Mane's best option against Clodsire and Eternatus. Alternatively, Mystical Fire can be used, being Flutter Mane's best option against Pokemon like Zacian-C and being boosted under sun. Power Gem is extremely valuable coverage, allowing it to OHKO offensive and defensive Ho-Oh after a bit of chip. Tera Fairy boosts Moonblast, allowing Flutter Mane to hit damage thresholds like 2HKOing Calm Mind Kyogre and Ting-Lu after a slight amount of chip while giving it a useful resistance to Dark-type attacks like Chien-Pao and Kingambit's Sucker Punch, although it removes its immunity to Extreme Speed. Tera Stellar is an option, giving Flutter Mane a one-time boost to any of its attacks, allowing it to outright OHKO any Ho-Oh variant while still retaining its valuable immunity to Extreme Speed. However, it is worthless after Flutter Mane uses a move, as that move will then not be boosted for the rest of the game.

When using Flutter Mane, Koraidon is a near-obligatory partner; Koraidon sets up sun, which enables Protosynthesis, as well as pivoting Flutter Mane into Pokemon it can beat like Landorus-T, opposing Koraidon, and Necrozma-DM. Other pivots like Miraidon and Landorus-T give Flutter Mane a safe opportunity to come into the field and wallbreak safely. Offensive Pokemon like Extreme Killer Arceus, Deoxys-A, and Kyogre all appreciate Flutter Mane wearing down their checks like Necrozma-DM and Miraidon. Physical attackers like Zacian-C, Groudon, and Ho-Oh make it difficult for Flutter Mane to come in safely and wallbreak; Pokemon that can take on these threats like one's own Ho-Oh, Necrozma-DM, and Arceus-Water all make good partners. Spikes support from Clodsire and Ting-Lu can give Flutter Mane extra support and chip Arceus into the range of Tera Fairy-boosted Moonblast. Flutter Mane has a terrible matchup against Sticky Web teams, as it has terrible bulk and is forced to gain a Special Attack boost from Protosynthesis when affected by Sticky Web, so partners like Extreme Killer Arceus and Calyrex-I can ease the matchup. Flutter Mane covers the Fairy-type teamslot on teams, giving them flexibility with picking an Arceus forme and Tera types.

movesets.name: Life Orb
movesets.description:
This set takes advantage of Flutter Mane's great strength and coverage to become a fearsome wallbreaker. Power Gem lets Flutter Mane destroy Ho-Oh, an otherwise perfect counter to Flutter Mane, but has very little practical use otherwise. Calm Mind lets Flutter Mane reliably break through defensive Arceus formes like Arceus-Ground and Arceus-Fairy for the benefit of teammates like Koraidon and Miraidon. Psyshock hits Clodsire and Eternatus, while Mystical Fire hits Zacian-C, but both have little practical use beyond hitting their intended targets. Tera Fairy is the preferred Tera type with Calm Mind. Tera Stellar is preferred when not running Calm Mind, as Flutter Mane's coverage moves can struggle to OHKO their intended targets. For example, Ho-Oh and Zacian-C can normally survive Power Gem and Mystical Fire, respectively, from full HP. However, with Tera Stellar, Flutter Mane's coverage moves are favored to OHKO these Pokemon. Tera Stellar is also useful for boosting Moonblast's power while keeping Flutter Mane's immunity to Extreme Speed from Extreme Killer Arceus, allowing Flutter Mane to pick it off from higher HP.

Choice Scarf Koraidon is Flutter Mane's best friend, as Koraidon provides Flutter Mane with sun and pivot support. Koraidon also appreciates Flutter Mane threatening Koraidon's checks for it, like Landorus-T and Ho-Oh. Another good partner is Miraidon, which can work with Flutter Mane to overwhelm shared checks such as Arceus-Ground and Arceus-Fairy. Spikes support from Gliscor and Ting-Lu are generally good for wallbreakers like Flutter Mane, but Flutter Mane in particular enjoys Spikes weakening its checks, as it's not easy to revenge kill courtesy of its impressive Speed and good defensive typing. Thus, Spikes allows Flutter Mane to continue being threatening even against fast-paced offensive teams, especially as its low bulk makes it somewhat difficult to safely get on the field; it can also be forced out by Pokemon like Zacian-C if not carrying Mystical Fire. Entry hazard control in the form of Giratina-O's Defog is also an option to increase Flutter Mane's longevity, as otherwise Flutter Mane gets worn down very quickly by entry hazards and Life Orb recoil.

movesets.name: Choice Specs (Fairy)
movesets.description:
Choice Specs Flutter Mane is an incredible wallbreaker for Fairy teams, making use of its blazing Speed and high Special Attack to easily remove threats to Fairy such as Gholdengo and Raging Bolt. Moonblast disposes of foes such as Raging Bolt and Choice Specs Greninja, along with 2HKOing would-be checks such as specially defensive Ting-Lu and Hisuian Goodra after minor chip damage. Shadow Ball handles Ghost- and Psychic-type threats such as Spectrier, Gholdengo, Pecharunt, and Galarian Slowking while also being Flutter Mane's best option against Steel-types such as Iron Treads and Heatran. Thunderbolt deals with Water- and Flying-types such as Toxapex, Pelipper, and Moltres. Finally, Power Gem checks Fire-types like Ogerpon-H and Volcarona, alongside Articuno. Alternatively, Psyshock can be run to better deal with special walls such as Clodsire and Blissey.

Iron Valiant serves as a great offensive complement to Flutter Mane, breaking through special walls and Steel-types such as Blissey, Hisuian Goodra, and Heatran with Close Combat, along with using coverage such as Ice Punch to check foes like Gliscor and specially defensive Clodsire. Iron Valiant can also opt for Choice Scarf sets to get the jump on checks to Flutter Mane such as Choice Specs Dragapult and Choice Scarf Gholdengo with Knock Off. Klefki can provide dual screens and Spikes support, making attempts to remove Flutter Mane less effective and wearing down special walls like Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra. Klefki's secondary Steel typing also makes it capable of coming in on Poison- and Steel-types like Sneasler and Scizor and threatening them with Thunder Wave and Foul Play, respectively. Primarina and Azumarill are both capable of checking Fire-type threats like Volcarona and Heatran for Flutter Mane. Primarina also provides a strong anti-Steel threat capable of handling Gholdengo and Corviknight after a Calm Mind. Azumarill can break through special walls like Water Absorb Clodsire and Empoleon and cripple others such as Articuno after a Belly Drum. Hatterene helps keep Flutter Mane healthy by preventing entry hazards from going up with Magic Bounce and can use Nuzzle to slow down Choice Scarf threats like Meowscarada and Enamorus. Hatterene can also pressure Poison-types such as Clodsire and Toxapex with Psyshock. Choice Scarf Enamorus can provide Healing Wish for Flutter Mane should its HP fall too low, along with outspeeding and removing unboosted Dragapult and Choice Scarf Great Tusk. Alternatively, Enamorus can run an Expert Belt set to better handle Steel teams, making it superior at checking Hisuian Goodra and Gholdengo.

movesets.name: Choice Specs (Ghost)
movesets.description:
Flutter Mane is the premier Choice Specs user on Ghost teams thanks to its amazing Special Attack and Speed, outpacing Pokemon like Greninja and Gengar, with immense coverage giving it tools for every situation. Moonblast is both Flutter Mane's strongest move and can remove problematic Dark- and Dragon-types like Greninja, Hydreigon, and Archaludon with ease. Shadow Ball gives Flutter Mane a STAB option into Fairy-resistant foes like Amoonguss and allows it to threaten slower Ghost-type threats like Gholdengo and Sinistcha. Thunderbolt shocks Water- and Flying-types like Toxapex, Empoleon, Corviknight, and Enamorus. Finally, Power Gem shatters problematic Ice- and Fire-types including Alolan Ninetales, Frosmoth, Ogerpon-H, and Volcarona.

Spikes support from the likes of Brambleghast and Froslass helps chip down special walls such as Alolan Muk, Hisuian Goodra, and Ting-Lu that could otherwise threaten Flutter Mane. Brambleghast can also provide Rapid Spin support to give Flutter Mane safe entry and can threaten bulky Water- and Ground-types like Swampert, Gastrodon, and Clodsire. Froslass, meanwhile, can prevent the placement of entry hazards and Defog with Taunt. Gholdengo assists Flutter Mane by taking Steel-type attacks from the likes of Scizor, Corviknight, and Hisuian Goodra, status from the likes of Blissey, and Defog from the likes of Corviknight; in return, Gholdengo appreciates Power Gem support to remove Fire-types like Volcarona and Ogerpon-H that threaten it. Pecharunt, thanks to its high physical bulk, can withstand hits from the likes of Iron Hands, Ogerpon-W, and Scizor and threaten back with Malignant Chain to spread status to weaken walls or Foul Play to clear physical attackers away. Pecharunt can also safely bring in Flutter Mane thanks to Parting Shot. Sinistcha can help to take on the several Water- and Ground-types of the tier, including Barraskewda, Swampert, and Clodsire, along with being able to use Matcha Gotcha to burn physical attackers that can threaten Flutter Mane such as Alolan Muk and Iron Treads. Ceruledge benefits Flutter Mane by being able to use Bitter Blade to remove problematic Steel-types like Scizor and Magnezone along with being able to use Poltergeist to hit hard into special walls like Clodsire and Heatran. Ceruledge can also check opposing Flutter Mane and Dragapult thanks to Shadow Sneak. Dragapult enjoys Flutter Mane being able to break physical walls, including Archaludon, Great Tusk, and Overqwil. In return, Dragapult can wear down special walls like Alolan Muk and Iron Hands with its powerful STAB moves so Flutter Mane can effortlessly remove them. If wielding a Choice Scarf, Dragapult can also check opposing Choice Scarf threats like Meowscarada, Roaring Moon, and Hoopa-U, which all pose a significant threat to Flutter Mane.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Ghost)
movesets.description:
When opting for a Choice Scarf, Flutter Mane becomes incredible speed control for Ghost teams, beating out other fast threats such as unboosted Dragapult, Choice Scarf Meowscarada, and weakened Sand Rush Excadrill. Moonblast removes Dark- and Dragon-types such as Greninja, Roaring Moon, and Garchomp. Shadow Ball provides an excellent tool to clean up opposing Ghost teams. Thunderbolt zaps Flying- and Water-types such as Skarmory, non-Assault Vest Tornadus-T, and Toxapex. Finally, Flutter Mane has a lot of potential tools to play around with: Energy Ball catches Swampert and Gastrodon attempting to switch in on Thunderbolt while also greatly threatening Mamoswine, Psyshock handles ​switch-ins from the likes of Clodsire, and Power Gem removes Volcarona, Moltres, and Articuno.

Without the immense threat level of Choice Specs, Flutter Mane will need further help breaking through checks, making Spikes support from the likes of Brambleghast and Froslass necessary to wear down special walls such as Hisuian Goodra, Ting-Lu, and Alolan Muk. Brambleghast can also provide removal with Rapid Spin and assist in removing Ground- and Water-types like Hippowdon and Primarina. Pecharunt can pivot Flutter Mane in with Parting Shot while also spreading Toxic poison through Malignant Chain to wear down bulkier threats like Assault Vest Iron Hands. Ceruledge and physical Dragapult variants break through special walls for Flutter Mane such as Blissey and Hisuian Goodra. Ceruledge can also take on Steel-types such as Corviknight and Scizor. Nasty Plot Gholdengo can wear down special walls such as Alolan Muk, allowing Flutter Mane to easily clean up. It also switches in on priority such as Scizor's Bullet Punch and Mamoswine's Ice Shard. Hisuian Zoroark can enter ​on attempts to remove Flutter Mane from Shadow Sneak Brambleghast and Ceruledge and threaten them back with Poltergeist, along with using Illusion to trick opposing special walls like Blissey and Ting-Lu into taking a Low Kick.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description:
• Flutter Mane's blistering Speed and Special Attack along with its powerful unresisted STAB combination exerts an oppressive amount of pressure on most teams, making it one of the premier offensive Pokemon in the format.

  • Mystical Fire: Mystical Fire scorches the many Steel-types such as Zacian-C. It also heavily disrupts enemy special attackers.

  • Power Gem: Power Gem gets a bit of extra damage against Fire-types like Ogerpon-H and Ho-Oh, which can be relevant when using Tera Stellar.

  • Substitute: Calm Mind + Substitute is a classic duo that greatly assists Flutter Mane's setup attempts, allowing it to set up in-front of Thunder Wave users such as Arceus. Even without Calm Mind, it can save Flutter Mane from devastating uses of Thunder Wave from the likes of Archaludon.

  • Taunt: Taunt is hugely disruptive against a variety of support Pokemon, such as Dondozo, Ting-Lu, and Glimmora.

Other Options

  • Stellar Tera Blast: With Tera Stellar, Tera Blast can be some good insurance against Pokemon with unpredictable Terastallization options, but the Special Attack drop doesn't gel well with Booster Energy.

  • Draining Kiss: When using extremely bulky Flutter Mane variants, Draining Kiss can be paired with Calm Mind to keep it around much longer. However, Tera Fairy is highly recommended when using this, as Draining Kiss is otherwise very weak.

Items

  • Booster Energy: Flutter Mane's incredible Speed is put to good use, outspeeding almost everything in the metagame with the major exceptions being Booster Energy Iron Bundle and Choice Scarf Calyrex-S.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash patches up Flutter Mane's poor physical bulk, giving it new revenge kill chances.

EV Spreads

  • All of these EV spreads are designed to give Flutter Mane a Speed Boost with Protosynthesis.

  • 4 HP / 108 Defense / 140 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid: The Defense investment usually allows Flutter Mane to survive Sucker Punch from Adamant Chien-Pao. To require Adamant Chien-Pao to get a critical hit to OHKO Flutter Mane with Sucker Punch, an EV spread of 4 HP / 124 Def / 124 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe can also be used.

  • 116 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA / 4 SpD / 132 Spe with Timid: This EV spread outspeeds Jolly Roaring Moon and survives an opposing Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball without Terastallization. In addition, Life Orb Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak has a fairly low chance of OHKOing, and Iron Bundle fails to KO with the combination of Hydro Pump and Freeze Dry.

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Timid: If using Focus Sash, this simple spread is best for maximizing Speed and power. Note that this spread's vulnerability to priority makes it a poor fit for Booster Energy variants.

  • 236 HP / 252 Def / 20 Spe with Bold: This extremely defensive spread allows Flutter Mane to survive Tera Dark Life Orb Jolly Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch without needing to Terastallize itself, while still outspeeding Choice Scarf Jolly Landorus-T and Gouging Fire after Booster Energy.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: While Flutter Mane benefits from Terastallization, it's generally flexible enough to go without it.

  • Stellar: Flutter Mane boosting all of its offensive moves once gives it good offensive flexibility, especially since it retains the important immunity to Extreme Speed.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy makes Moonblast a potent sweeping move, while reducing damage against Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch and Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak.

  • Water: Tera Water is handy for giving a resistance to Steel, Ice, and Fire, giving improved matchups against Scizor, Ting-Lu, Chien-Pao, and Chi-Yu.

  • Electric: In addition to resisting Bullet Punch, Tera Electric protects Flutter Mane from the dreaded Thunder Wave and Glare!

  • Fire: Tera Fire gives Flutter Mane an offensive and defensive edge against Scizor, though the weakness to Urshifu-R's Aqua Jet is quite unwelcome.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
• Thanks to its high Special Attack and Speed, Flutter Mane is a devastating wallbreaker, outspeeding and blowing holes in bulky metagame threats like Dragonite and Ting-Lu!

  • Power Gem: Power Gem is recommended to hit Ho-Oh and Ogerpon-H for super effective damage.

  • Mystical Fire versus Psyshock: Mystical Fire allows Flutter Mane to hit Steel-types like Zacian-C for huge damage while also nerfing the power of special attackers, although Psyshock can be used against Poison-types like Glimmora and Sneasler.

  • Perish Song: Perish Song is another alternative that can be used as an anti-setup option to counter team archetypes like Baton Pass.

Other Options

  • Tera Blast: Tera Blast in conjunction with Tera Stellar can be used to make Flutter Mane a check to surprise Terastallizations from Urshifu-R or Dragonite.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt can be used to more reliably threaten Dondozo, especially with Tera Stellar or Tera Electric.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 108 Def / 140 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid: This EV spread allows Flutter Mane to survive Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch before Terastallization while also maximizing Flutter Mane's Speed stat.

  • 4 HP / 52 Def / 212 SpA / 4 SpD / 212 Spe with Modest: This EV spread doesn't outspeed Arceus, but in exchange Flutter Mane OHKOes maximum HP Ogerpon-H with Tera Stellar Power Gem. The defensive investment survives an Aqua Jet from a +2 Adamant Urshifu-R.

  • 116 HP / 204 Def / 116 SpA / 4 SpD / 68 Spe with Modest: This EV spread only outspeeds up to the Jolly Urshifu formes but maximizes Flutter Mane's ability to take hits, such as surviving a Tera Dark Sucker Punch from an Adamant Urshifu-S after Stealth Rock damage, surviving Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash, and having a 93% chance to survive Surging Strikes from Adamant Urshifu-R.

  • 252 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid: This is an alternate spread that can be used to maximize Flutter Mane's damage output.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Flutter Mane already has a stunning type combination, which doesn't need much of a boost. However, the Tera type can be used to boost Flutter Mane's offensive capabilities even further.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy gives Flutter Mane a boost on Moonblast and helps it against Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S Sucker Punch.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar gives Flutter Mane a one-time nuke to secure knockouts and works especially well with Tera Blast.

  • Electric: Tera Electric in conjunction with Thunderbolt can OHKO Dondozo and Primarina, as well as providing Flutter Mane with a paralysis immunity.

  • Water: Tera Water is a defensive option that patches up Flutter Mane's Steel-type weakness against foes like Archaludon and Scizor, as well as resisting Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes.

movesets.name: Offensive Support
movesets.description:
• Flutter Mane utilizes high Speed and Thunder Wave to become a status spreader and sweeper.

  • Hex versus Shadow Ball: Hex is normally preferred for dealing massive damage after a successful Thunder Wave. Shadow Ball can be used if consistent damage is more desirable and is almost always the stronger option against Gholdengo.

  • Taunt: Taunt is a great complement to Thunder Wave, shutting down opposing disruption and setup.

  • Pain Split: Pain Split can be used after a KO to heavily disrupt the next target and possibly stall out weaker attacks.

  • Mystical Fire: Defense-invested Flutter Mane can live unboosted Bullet Punch from Scizor and hit it back hard with Mystical Fire.

Other Options

  • Substitute: When paired with full paralysis chances and Pain Split, Flutter Mane can live for much longer than expected and snag some sneaky KOs. The main drawback is that Flutter Mane can only run one attack, usually Moonblast.

  • Calm Mind: Booster Energy sets can still make great use of Calm Mind. It is possible to get free setup turns thanks to full paralysis, but be aware that this is more of an occasional bonus than a consistent strategy to rely on.

Items

  • Booster Energy: With the Speed increase from Booster Energy, it is nearly guaranteed that Flutter Mane can cripple something.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash can be used with more offensive spreads, and is particularly strong against already boosted opponents.

  • Jaboca Berry: Jaboca Berry's damage is a sneaky option against physical attackers. It allows Flutter Mane to cleanly beat Focus Sash Chien-Pao and Urshifu in a single turn, while making the combination of Thunder Wave into Hex much more potent into offensive Dragonite.

EV Spreads

  • 236 HP / 252 Def / 20 Spe with Bold or Timid: This spread gives great survivability, surviving unboosted Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and unboosted Bullet Punch from Scizor. 20 Speed EVs ensures that Booster Energy boosts Speed, outrunning Choice Scarf users like Landorus-T. Bold is preferable to maximize bulk, but Timid is still viable to get the jump on other “slow” Flutter Mane and outrun Choice Scarf Urshifu.

  • 4 HP / 108 Def / 140 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid: This spread allows Flutter Mane to be more offensively oriented while still maintaining some bulk, almost always surviving Adamant Chien-Pao's unboosted Sucker Punch.

  • 4 Def / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Timid: A full offensive spread can be used if opting for Focus Sash.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Flutter Mane's high Speed and support options allow it to disrupt with ease. Terastallization is therefore only needed for specific matchups where maintaining momentum is important.

  • Water: Tera Water resists Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash, and gains a Steel-type resistance for the Zacian-C and Scizor matchups.

  • Electric: Tera Electric prevents Flutter Mane from being paralyzed itself–an important consideration for the mirror–while still giving a pivotal Steel-type resistance.

movesets.name: Charm
movesets.description:
• The combination of Charm and Pain Split turns Flutter Mane into a devastating control option, massively crippling opposing offensive threats and healing itself with the combination of Pain Split and Draining Kiss.

  • Calm Mind versus coverage: Calm Mind allows Flutter Mane to maintain its role as a sweeper by increasing its damage output while simultaneously reinforcing its longevity. However, this leaves Flutter Mane quite vulnerable to Steel-types, so Shadow Ball and Mystical Fire are reasonable alternatives.

  • Draining Kiss versus Moonblast: Moonblast's far superior damage output is a great option versus more defensive teams, while Draining Kiss supplies superior lasting power against more offensive teams and is a great fit for Tera Fairy.

EV Spreads

  • 124 HP / 252 Def / 132 Spe with Timid: The chosen EVs ensure that Flutter Mane will always outspeed Jolly Booster Energy Roaring Moon. Maximum Defense investment gets the most out of Charm with the rest placed into HP.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Since this Flutter Mane is trying to defeat unexpected physical threats one-on-one, Terastallization is great at patching up some matchups that Charm can't on its own, even if it's not required for this set to work.

  • Water: Tera Water gives Flutter Mane a very useful resistance to Steel, Ice, and Fire, giving it improved matchups against Zacian-C, Ting-Lu, Chien-Pao, and Chi-Yu.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy Further boosts Moonblast's impressive damage output while removing Flutter Mane's Ghost weakness.

  • Electric: Tera Electric not only gives a useful Bullet Punch resistance against Scizor, but it also prevents common paralysis spreaders like opposing Flutter Mane, Archaludon, and Mimikyu from crippling Flutter Mane.

strategies.overview:
• Flutter Mane's extraordinary Special Attack and Speed combined with its fantastic offensive typing makes it one of the most effective cleaners in the format, 2HKOing the majority of the metagame. Flutter Mane can also play a supportive role for its team thanks to Icy Wind and Speed Booster Energy.

  • Offensive sets appreciate Pokemon that bring speed control like Latias and Tornadus, as well as Pokemon that provide it with longevity like Incineroar and Amoonguss. Supportive sets instead become the speed control and help support slower offensive Pokemon like Urshifu-R and Chi-Yu. Chi-Yu works particularly well as a partner, bolstering Flutter Mane's damage with Beads of Ruin and checking Steel-types like Kingambit while Flutter Mane takes care of Fighting-types like Urshifu-R in return.

  • Bulky Assault Vest users that can take a boosted Moonblast and OHKO Flutter Mane in response like Kingambit and Rillaboom are some of its toughest matchups. Flutter Mane also faces issues into faster threats like Chien-Pao and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. Additionally, redirectors like Indeedee-F and Ogerpon-W mitigate its damage output when on the field.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description:
• Flutter Mane is an effective cleaner thanks to Moonblast, which is its strongest STAB move, and Dazzling Gleam, which provides spread damage.

  • Special Attack Booster Energy is Flutter Mane's strongest boosting item if it wants to keep Protect. Fairy Feather can be used instead, allowing it to retain its offensive boosts when switching at the cost of damage.

  • The EV spread is built to survive an Ice Spinner from Jolly Chien-Pao and to outspeed Tornadus, with the remaining EVs boosting Flutter Mane's Special Attack

  • Flutter Mane appreciates Tera Fairy to further boost its damage on Moonblast and Dazzling Gleam . This also removes its Ghost weakness and makes it resist Dark-type attacks, allowing it to better deal with opposing Flutter Mane and survive a potential Sucker Punch from Pokemon like Kingambit.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
• Choice Specs is Flutter Mane's strongest boosting item and allows it to do immediate damage.

  • Flutter Mane utilizes Icy Wind as a speed control option and as coverage to threaten chipped Landorus. Thunderbolt and Power Gem are strong coverage options for important Pokemon like Tera Water Urshifu-R and Incineroar, respectively.

  • The above spread allows Flutter Mane to survive a Surging Strikes from a Choice Scarf Urshifu-R while outspeeding Adamant Chien-Pao. The remaining EVs are used to maximise its Special Attack.

  • Flutter Mane takes advantage of Tera Fairy by removing its Ghost weakness and giving it a Dark resistance, allowing it to better deal with opposing Flutter Mane and survive a potential Sucker Punch from Pokemon like Chien-Pao. Tera Fairy also allows Flutter Mane to secure an OHKO on Tera Water Urshifu-R.

movesets.name: Speed-Boosting Support
movesets.description:
• Flutter Mane requires Icy Wind to accomplish its role as speed control, forcing it to pick between Dazzling Gleam and Moonblast.

  • Speed Booster Energy allows Flutter Mane to outspeed the majority of the metagame.

  • With Booster Energy, Flutter Mane can outspeed opposing Chien-Pao at -1 and Modest Gholdengo in Tailwind. The defensive investment lets it survive Adamant Chien-Pao's Ice Spinner and Gholdengo's Make It Rain.

  • Tera Fairy is appreciated to gain more of an offensive presence and helps against opposing Flutter Mane, as Speed Booster Energy Flutter Mane is unable to OHKO opposing Flutter Mane with Shadow Ball.

movesets.name: Defensive Support
movesets.description:
• Flutter Mane uses its high Speed to spread paralysis, slow down foes with Icy Wind, and Taunt foes before they can move. Due to its solid bulk, it is hard to remove, letting it stay on the field longer and support its team. In some matchups, Flutter Mane can choose to spam Thunder Wave, with the chance of a full paralysis combining with Flutter Mane's bulk to give slower paced teams a rough time.

  • Thunder Wave and Icy Wind give Flutter Mane different options for speed control; Thunder Wave lowers the Speed stats of foes more, while Icy Wind can threaten Landorus and break Focus Sashes. Taunt shuts down Trick Room and Amoonguss. Pain Split is an option over either speed control option to give Flutter Mane some healing while also taking advantage of its low HP stat to weaken foes.

  • Booster Energy allows Flutter Mane to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame while letting it outspeed slower Choice Scarf users like Adamant Urshifu-R and Modest Chi-Yu.

  • The HP and Defense investment allow Flutter Mane to survive Surging Strikes from Mystic Water Urshifu-R almost all of the time. By running a Bold nature, Flutter Mane gives up the opportunity to outspeed Speed Booster Energy Roaring Moon and opposing Flutter Mane, but the bulk it gains makes it difficult to remove without heavy commitment.

  • Tera Grass allows Flutter Mane to resist Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and Grass-type moves from Rillaboom, letting it get off another attack. Tera Grass also gives Flutter Mane an immunity to Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss, letting it Taunt Amoonguss's partner or not have to worry about predictably using Taunt each time Amoonguss is on the field. Tera Fairy boosts the damage of Moonblast, which can partially make up for the damage lost by investing heavily in HP and Defense.

movesets.name: Offensive Speed Control
movesets.description:
Flutter Mane's excellent Ghost / Fairy typing that offers an immunity to Fake Out, its Protosynthesis ability and Booster Energy allowing it to gain a Speed boost, and its vast movepool including Speed-reducing moves such as Icy Wind and Thunder Wave help Flutter Mane function as an excellent speed control Pokemon in Regulation G. Flutter Mane is especially effective against Pokemon that rely on their speed, such as Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Calyrex-S, as it can threaten to OHKO or slow them down before they move. Taunt can be used instead of Shadow Ball to shut down support Pokemon like Amoonguss and Clefairy, as well as prevent Terapagos from setting up. Flutter Mane can also opt for Thunder Wave to reduce the Speed of Clear Amulet and Covert Cloak Pokemon such as Koraidon and Calyrex-S. Icy Wind is mandatory for Flutter Mane to play as speed control, slowing down both opposing Pokemon while also breaking Focus Sash from the likes of Chien-Pao and the Urshifu formes. Booster Energy allows Flutter Mane to outspeed the entire metagame and become a stronger form of speed control. The EV spread enables Flutter Mane to survive strong physical attacks such as Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance, Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash, and almost always Adamant Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes. The Special Defense lets it take Volt Switch from Modest Choice Specs Miraidon and Blood Moon from Ursaluna-B. Meanwhile, the Speed investment lets Flutter Mane outspeed neutral nature base 135 Speed Pokemon like Miraidon and Chien-Pao. Tera Fairy is great on Flutter Mane to shed its weakness to Ghost-type attacks such as Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S and boost its damage output, allowing Flutter Mane to threaten a potential OHKO on Miraidon and ensure a 2HKO on Raging Bolt.

Flutter Mane struggles against bulky physical attackers like Assault Vest Rillaboom and Iron Hands, which can sponge its attacks, don't mind becoming slower, and threaten an OHKO in return. Zacian-C and Zamazenta-C are major issues in a similar way, but they don't enjoy having their Speed reduced. Flutter Mane also struggles to keep up with more immediate speed control, specifically Prankster Tailwind from Tornadus and Whimsicott, that may allow slower Pokemon like Urshifu-R and Miraidon to threaten it. Flutter Mane pairs well with a variety of Pokemon, namely offensive Pokemon that can utilize its speed control. Chi-Yu exploits this especially well, threatening Zacian-C, Zamazenta-C, and Rillaboom with Heat Wave and Overheat. Chi-Yu also makes up for Flutter Mane's lack of offensive investment with Beads of Ruin and appreciates Flutter Mane's ability to threaten Dragon-types. Choice Specs Terapagos is an excellent asset for this duo, as it takes advantage of how often Flutter Mane and Chi-Yu can force Terastallization. Zamazenta-C can protect Flutter Mane from threatening spread moves such as Astral Barrage and Glacial Lance from the Calyrex formes. Terapagos and Zamazenta-C also appreciate Flutter Mane's speed control making up for their mediocre speed tiers, and its Fairy typing that threatens Koraidon.

movesets.name: Glass Cannon
movesets.description:
Flutter Mane is a supportive special attacker that functions well on sun teams. Since Flutter Mane is immune to Fake Out, it can ignore the threat of Fake Out to use Taunt on Pokemon such as Calyrex-I or Amoonguss as well as being able to attack without having to fear the chip damage that the move does. Flutter Mane can use support moves such as Taunt over Shadow Ball to prevent opposing Pokemon like Calyrex-I or Amoonguss from setting Trick Room or using moves like Spore, respectively. When paired with Pokemon that set sun such as Koraidon or Groudon, Flutter Mane can use Protosynthesis to boost its Speed and use Icy Wind as a form of speed control, outspeeding and slowing down Pokemon such as Calyrex-S. Dazzling Gleam gives Flutter Mane a spread option that it can boost with Terastallization. Focus Sash lets Flutter Mane live a hit without needing to invest EVs in bulk. Tera Fairy and Stellar both allow Flutter Mane to OHKO Raging Bolt; Tera Stellar allows Shadow Ball to pick up KOs like those against all opposing Flutter Mane. However, Tera Fairy is more consistent, since it can use Fairy-type STAB moves without worrying about losing the boost.

Choice Scarf Urshifu-R threatens Flutter Mane when paired with Pokemon such as Tornadus or Pelipper that can set rain for it, removing both Flutter Mane's Speed boost and the sun. Assault Vest Rillaboom can take Flutter Mane's attacks, threaten it with Wood Hammer, and finish it off on the subsequent turn with Grassy Glide. Flutter Mane pairs well with Pokemon that can redirect attacks away from it such as Ogerpon and Amoonguss, since this allows it to maintain its Focus Sash and stay on the field longer. In addition to redirecting attacks, Amoonguss matches up well into Urshifu-R. Raging Bolt can remove Pokemon such as Urshifu-R that threaten Flutter Mane while also reliably switching into Rillaboom's Wood Hammer and Grassy Glide. Chi-Yu also benefits from Icy Wind speed control and threatens Rillaboom while also boosting Flutter Mane's damage with Beads of Ruin.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
Flutter Mane works well as an offensive threat due to its great offensive typing and Speed, allowing it to outspeed most of the metagame and do notable damage to Pokemon like Koraidon, Miraidon, and both Calyrex and Urshifu formes. Shadow Ball and Moonblast are strong STAB moves, and Dazzling Gleam provides strong spread damage. Power Gem provides good coverage for Fire-type Pokemon like Incineroar and Ogerpon-H, Taunt is a good way to shut down support Pokemon like Amoonguss and Farigiraf, and Icy Wind is great speed control. Choice Specs increases Flutter Mane's offense even further, as it can OHKO Pokemon such as Assault Vest Raging Bolt. The EV spread allows Flutter Mane to outspeed Chien-Pao, Koraidon, and Miraidon without Speed-boosting natures and live an Ice Spinner from Adamant Chien-Pao. Tera Fairy is great both offensively and defensively, as Flutter Mane could output more damage, resist Dark-type moves from the likes of Chien-Pao and Urshifu, and give Flutter Mane a neutrality to Ghost, allowing it to survive an Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S.

Pokemon that can outspeed and OHKO Flutter Mane, like Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Calyrex-S, and Pokemon that can survive Flutter Mane STAB moves like Amoonguss are good checks to Flutter Mane. Flutter Mane's physical fraility is also a huge weakness, mostly fainting against a plethora of physical moves. Incineroar is a good teammate for Flutter Mane, as Intimidate can help Flutter Mane shore up its poor Defense while also having a resistance against Dark- and Ghost-type moves. Pokemon with the ability to set up the sun like Groudon and Koraidon are also good teammates for Flutter Mane, as it allows Protosynthesis to activate and heighten Flutter Mane's Speed stat.

movesets.name: Glass Cannon
movesets.description:
Set Details

  • Flutter Mane's role is to capitalize on the Speed boost provided by its sun setter and to offer speed control while pressuring opposing Pokemon to Terastallize with its coverage. In sun, it outspeeds major offensive threats like Miraidon, Koraidon, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, and Calyrex-S, threatening them with its STAB moves.
  • Shadow Ball is useful for threatening Lunala, Calyrex-S, and opposing Flutter Mane more effectively. Icy Wind is Flutter Mane's preferred speed control option, as it slows down both foes—enabling Koraidon, which delivers far greater damage output, to clean up more easily. It also helps break Focus Sash.
  • Taunt is a useful tool for shutting down opposing Trick Room setters like Lunala and Calyrex-I, blocking Spore from Amoonguss and Brute Bonnet, and preventing setup from threats like Terapagos. Taunt has niche uses such as stopping Parting Shot from Incineroar and preventing Protect and redirection on turns after Taunt is used, allowing your team to apply as much offensive pressure as possible before the sun runs out.
  • Becuase it usually has Koraidon to set the sun for its Protosynthesis Speed boost, this Flutter Mane set can run full offensive investment and a Focus Sash instead of Booster Energy. Focus Sash is valuable for this more offensive Flutter Mane build due to its fragility, especially on the physical side.
  • Tera Normal is mainly used as a countermeasure for Calyrex-S to gain an immunity to its Astral Barrage, though it can also be useful to gain an immunity to Lunala's Moongeist Beam. Tera Fairy is used to boost Moonblast's power, which lets it OHKO non-Assault Vest Miraidon outright as well as Tera Dragon Zamazenta-C and Brute Bonnet most of the time. Tera Stellar carries a similar benefit to Tera Fairy in terms of Moonblast OHKOs, though only on its first use, and it can also enable Shadow Ball to score surprise OHKOs on Pokemon such as Shadow Shield Lunala when Chi-Yu is on the field.

Teambuilding

  • Bulky Restricted Pokemon like Zamazenta-C and Ho-Oh check this offensive Flutter Mane set, as they can comfortably take its hits and strike back with moves like Behemoth Bash or Heavy Slam and Sacred Fire, respectively.
  • Priority move users such as Chien-Pao with Sucker Punch or Ice Shard and Rillaboom with Grassy Glide hinder the effectiveness of the set by breaking Focus Sash or picking up the KO when it is down to 1 HP before it can attack.
  • Flutter Mane pairs well with Koraidon because it sets up the sun, triggering Flutter Mane's Protosynthesis Speed boost. In turn, Flutter Mane can provide speed control with Icy Wind, so Koraidon is able to outspeed Pokemon like Calyrex-S and threaten OHKOs with Close Combat or Flare Blitz.
  • Flutter Mane is commonly paired with Choice Scarf Chi-Yu to round out a sun core because both Flutter Mane and Chi-Yu exert fast, immediate offensive pressure, with Chi-Yu's ability helping bolster Flutter Mane's damage output.
  • Lastly, Pokemon with redirection such as Brute Bonnet and Indeedee-F can help Flutter Mane by protecting it from priority attacks like Raging Bolt's Thunderclap and Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch, particularly when Flutter Mane is taken down to 1 HP.

strategies.outdated: This analysis was written before BH had a major shakeup. As such, the set(s) and comments may not be up-to-date.
strategies.overview: Flutter Mane is an effective fast attacker. A Ghost typing and good Speed let it effectively use Normalize + Entrainment as a disruption tool, while more offensive sets can benefit from Moongeist Beam for high damage against Ice Scales users like Ho-Oh; Normalize in particular makes Flutter Mane an effective entry hazard setter and check to setup threats like Eternatus and some Take Heart Arceus formes. Flutter Mane also benefits from low Attack and HP, the latter of which makes Pain Split a solid choice on utility sets that lets it chunk Blissey for good damage, and decent Special Defense lets it trade damage—albeit with a high cost—against faster foes like Mega Sceptile. However, Flutter Mane's offensive profile is notably throttled by Mega Audino and Arceus-Steel, two common walls that Flutter Mane struggles to break through. It also suffers from weaknesses to common status moves like Glare and Topsy-Turvy that can stall its progress, and it, in many cases, is forced to make risky decisions thanks to said status move weakness. Flutter Mane's weak Defense also means it can't afford to stay in on stray hits like Flip Turn much, either.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Flutter Mane's immunities to Dragon and Fighting mean it can use defensive abilities like Ice Scales and immunity abilities like Well-Baked Body and Levitate; however, this eats into damage output, making Magic Bounce users much more problematic. Flutter Mane can potentially use a Choice Specs set with either Beads of Ruin or Pixilate, but its damage falls short of competitors like Mega Alakazam, and it now struggles much more against RegenVest users. Flare Boost sets can act as potent sweepers with Nasty Plot and a built-in status immunity, but these suffer from high rates of residual damage.

Checks and Counters

Status: All Flutter Mane sets simply stop working when paralyzed; Normalize sets also falter to burn and poison. Common users also tend to carry moves like Ruination, like Chansey and Blissey, forcing Flutter Mane into unfavorable situations.

Steel-types: Arceus-Steel and Registeel resist Fairy and have good special bulk to take Ghost-type moves. The former threatens with Revelation Dance or Tachyon Cutter and can cut off Pain Split recovery with Good as Gold, while the latter threatens with Nuzzle or Gigaton Hammer. Dialga-O does not resist Fairy, but commonly uses Assault Vest, will always be carrying Revelation Dance or Doom Desire, both of which force Flutter Mane out and beat Normalize sets.

Revelation Dance and Judgment: These moves bypass Normalize, meaning that Flutter Mane essentially can't set up in front of them. Ice Scales Arceus formes also benefit from Flutter Mane still needing to use Entrainment to do meaningful damage.

Normal-types: Mega Audino, Blissey, and Meloetta all largely shut down Flutter Mane's direct damage and consistently carry Topsy-Turvy to offset Nasty Plot boosts. They tend to be fodder for Spikes, however, and only sparingly use Glare.

Magic Bounce: Magic Bounce users like Arceus-Poison and Clodsire blank most of Flutter Mane's status moves, including Spikes and Entrainment.

movesets.name: Utility
movesets.description:
Thanks to a combination of its great stat distribution and typing, this set turns Flutter Mane into an exceptional utility Pokemon capable of exerting long-term pressure. Magic Guard mitigates Life Orb recoil, poison damage, and entry hazard damage. Alternatively, Pixilate provides Flutter Mane with an extremely spammable STAB Boomburst, which, even without a boosting item, is capable of putting pressure to force special walls in, while Teravolt allows Flutter Mane to bypass Ice Scales and Magic Bounce. Pain Split synergizes phenomenally with Flutter Mane's low HP stat by allowing it to annoy common high-HP Pokemon like Eternatus, Blissey, and Chansey while also preventing Imposter users from freely recovering. Flutter Mane is an excellent Spikes setter with its solid longevity and many opportunities to switch in, and Spikes allows it to guarantee progress against more passive special walls like Mega Audino and Blissey. Astral Barrage gives Flutter Mane a way to severely threaten Arceus-Ghost and Solgaleo, and it further dissuades Imposter users. Knock Off is a great option to remove Assault Vest and Heavy-Duty Boots from checks, but it can be annoying to Imposter-proof. Topsy-Turvy provides more defensive utility, allowing Flutter Mane to handle boosting special attackers like Arceus formes easier. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Flutter Mane to ignore hazard damage, while Covert Cloak is useful against secondary effects from common moves like Mortal Spin and Nuzzle.

Utility Flutter Mane works well on balanced structures, though it can also perform on more offensive teams. Almost all offensive Pokemon appreciate Flutter Mane's support with Spikes. Additionally, physical wallbreakers benefit from Flutter Mane's low Attack reducing Strength Sap recovery from walls like Fur Coat Arceus formes and Zamazenta, while special wallbreakers enjoy Flutter Mane annoying special walls like Blissey and RegenVest Pokemon with Pain Split and Knock Off, respectively. Flutter Mane fits naturally into entry hazard-stacking and hazard-resilient compositions; the former appreciates its strong Spikes-setting capabilities and utility from Knock Off, while the latter eases the Imposter-proofing by being able to ignore Spikes from Imposter users. As a Spikes setter, Flutter Mane appreciates Steel-type teammates like Celesteela, Dialga-O, and Solgaleo that can block Mortal Spin and complement it defensively by switching into checks like Arceus-Steel. Imposter users generally dislike switching into Flutter Mane, but it still requires an Imposter-proof teammate such as Ho-Oh, Arceus-Steel, or RegenVest Celesteela depending on the moveset.

movesets.name: Normalize
movesets.description:
Normalize + Entrainment allows Flutter Mane to ignore most forms of direct damage, giving it free turns to set up or use its utility options. Judgment both ignores Normalize and allows Flutter Mane to attack with a STAB-boosted move without Imposter users being able to. Taunt shuts off annoyances like Glare and Parting Shot, and it additionally pairs well with all last-move options; Nasty Plot + Taunt makes it a solid sweeper with the rare ability to beat Topsy-Turvy users, Spikes is especially useful due to Entrainment beating all forms of entry hazard removal and forcing switches, and Thunder Cage + Taunt allows it to trap and remove targets that lack ways to damage it through Normalize. Pixie Plate has more consistent damage, while Spooky Plate is more threatening to foes like Arceus-Ghost and Imposter users.

Flutter Mane's best fit is on balance teams that can, depending on its set, either take advantage of its Spikes-setting ability or help pressure special walls that can beat Normalize. Ultra Necrozma makes a good candidate for its ability to threaten Arceus formes, which regularly carry Judgment, and Mega Audino with its mixed attacks. Slow pivots like RegenVest users are recommended, as Flutter Mane essentially stops working if hit with Knock Off or Mortal Spin; additionally, these Pokemon carrying Stone Axe benefit from Flutter Mane's tools to stop hazard removal and force switches. Reliable hazard removal or Wish support help Flutter Mane play more aggressively given its lack of recovery. A strong special wall like Blissey is also recommended as a check to rare Spooky Plate Imposter users, which can force Flutter Mane out. Flutter Mane's damage flatlines without its Plate, so Knock Off absorbers like Arceus formes are particularly helpful.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
• Other items like Farium Z can be considered if ran without Sun.
  • The given EVs allow Flutter Mane to live Life Orb Marshadow's Shadow Sneak while outspeeding Speed Boosted Gouging Fire and Landorus-T
